text:
maria: Hey team — customer (tenant=acme-corp) is getting repeated 429s when sending long-context chat requests to redwood-large-v2. Started after they increased history to ~12k tokens. Happens during peak (17:00-18:00 UTC). I've attached the raw curl and the 429 body below. Can someone help triage?

alex: can you paste the x-request-id from the 429 response + the exact payload size (input tokens + expected output tokens)?

maria: x-request-id: f2a3b6c9-9d12-4f5a-8b2e-7a1d3efc0b12. payload estimate: input ~11,600 tokens (chat history), expected output 400 tokens. Using model=redwood-large-v2, temp=0.2.

maria: curl sample:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"..."}, {"role":"user","content":"<~11.6k tokens of history>"}],"max_tokens":400}'
```

maria: 429 response body:```json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "message": "model redwood-large-v2: token throughput exceeded (TPM). try reducing context length or retrying later.",
  "request_id": "f2a3b6c9-9d12-4f5a-8b2e-7a1d3efc0b12"
}
```

support-bot: Ticket INC-2026 created for tenant acme-corp and assigned to eng-sre. :ticket:

ingrid: thanks — this looks like a classic TPM hit more than plain RPM. Important distinction for troubleshooting: RPM = requests/min (per-model), TPM = tokens/min (per-model). Long contexts blow up TPM quickly because input tokens count toward TPM. The platform also enforces a max concurrency per model which can produce 429s or queueing if exceeded.

alex: do we know the customer's plan? Dedicated vs hosted? If Dedicated with reserved capacity they'd usually bypass shared per-model TPM unless they've set a strict limit.

maria: they're on hosted, low-tier org. No dedicated reservation.

ingrid: steps to repro locally: 1) reproduce with a single thread request at the same token scale. 2) check response headers on 429 — we often include: `x-rate-limit-model-rpm-limit`, `x-rate-limit-model-rpm-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-model-tpm-limit`, `x-rate-limit-model-tpm-remaining`, `x-request-id`, and `x-rate-limit-reset` (unix secs). Example headers we saw: `x-rate-limit-model-rpm-limit: 60`, `x-rate-limit-model-rpm-remaining: 12`, `x-rate-limit-model-tpm-limit: 120000`, `x-rate-limit-model-tpm-remaining: 1500`.

alex: helpful. can you run a short python repro that mimics their shape? paste below.

maria: repro script (py):```python
import requests
URL = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
HEADERS = {'Authorization':'Bearer sk-REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json'}
PAYLOAD = {
  'model':'redwood-large-v2',
  'messages':[{'role':'system','content':'You are a helpful assistant.'}, {'role':'user','content':'X'*200000}],  # ~11k tokens dummy
  'max_tokens':400
}
resp = requests.post(URL, json=PAYLOAD, headers=HEADERS)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers.get('x-rate-limit-model-tpm-remaining'), resp.headers.get('x-rate-limit-model-tpm-limit'))
print(resp.text)
```

maria: running this locally produced a 429 after ~3 attempts during a simulated burst of 8 concurrent threads. Headers on 429: `x-rate-limit-model-tpm-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-model-rpm-remaining: 18`.

chris: summary of root causes we should consider: - TPM exceed because input tokens huge - RPM exceed during bursts if they spike requests - concurrency limit hit if many parallel long requests - per-tenant soft quotas on hosted tier (burst protection).

ingrid: mitigation recommendations to give customer: 1) trim chat history (keep recent N turns) or compress older turns to summaries before sending — biggest ROI. 2) use streaming/partial context or fetch embeddings for long-term memory and only include top-k relevant chunks. 3) add client-side exponential backoff with jitter for 429s (Retry-After from headers when present). 4) if long outputs are required, stagger requests or reduce concurrency.

alex: operational next steps for us: - confirm exact TPM/RPM limits for redwood-large-v2 for their org and collect 1 hour of server-side logs around f2a3b6c9-... - check if tenant crossed the per-model token budget for the minute and whether there was simultaneous spike from other services.

maria: I've attached logs to INC-2026 and included the request_id. Also attached the k6 load profile we used.

ingrid: one more note about context-length-related throttling: we sometimes enforce an internal per-request token ceiling (max_context_tokens) — requests that exceed that ceiling might be rejected outright with 400 or 413, but more commonly the platform lets the request through and then counts all tokens against TPM, which results in 429 if the rolling minute budget is exhausted. Ask the customer to check our response headers for a `x-context-tokens` header we include in debug mode.

chris: if customer needs higher sustained throughput for big contexts, propose Dedicated or a higher hosted tier — Dedicated gives you a separate pool and different limits. If they want a short-term lift, we can request a temporary quota bump, but we need the load profile and business justification.

maria: customer prefers immediate workaround — I'll send back recommended short-term changes: reduce context to 6k tokens, enable summarization, add retry/backoff. Also offered to run a focused repro with eng-sre during their peak tomorrow.

support-bot: INC-2026 updated: assigned to eng-sre, priority=P2, next touch Friday 17:30 UTC. :spiral_calendar:

alex: thanks — if eng-sre confirms it's TPM throttling we should return an internal note on how TPM is computed (rolling 60s window, tokens counted input+output, and small rounding behavior). I'll add that to the ticket.

maria: perfect. I'll message the customer with the mitigation steps and keep the ticket open until we have a repro and either a quota bump or a plan for Dedicated. :thumbsup:
